propositions.name: atoms_as_material_points
propositions.statement: The bodies studied by the physicist are ultimately composed of material points separated by intervals enormous in comparison with their dimensions.
propositions.quote: There also we should see material points, separated from one another by intervals, enormous in comparison with their dimensions, and describing orbits according to regular laws. These infinitesimal stars are the atoms.

propositions.name: central_forces_along_line
propositions.statement: The attraction or repulsion between atoms acts following the straight line which joins them and depends only on the distance.
propositions.quote: Like the stars proper, they attract or repel each other, and this attraction or this repulsion, following the straight line which joins them, depends only on the distance.

propositions.name: force_is_function_of_distance
propositions.statement: The force between two atoms is a definite function of the distance between them, characterized by an exponent.
propositions.quote: The law according to which this force varies as function of the distance is perhaps not the law of Newton, but it is an analogous law; in place of the exponent −2, we have probably a different exponent

propositions.name: distance_between_atoms_definite
propositions.statement: There is a definite distance between any two atoms that determines the force between them.
propositions.quote: the atoms of ether attract each other in the inverse ratio of the sixth power of the distance; and Maxwell himself, does he not say somewhere that the atoms of gases repel each other in the inverse ratio of the fifth power of the distance?

propositions.name: phenomenal_diversity_from_exponent
propositions.statement: The variety of physical phenomena, qualities, and sensations arises from the change of exponent in the force law between atoms.
propositions.quote: it is from this change of exponent that arises all the diversity of physical phenomena, the variety of qualities and of sensations, all the world, colored and sonorous, which surrounds us; in a word, all nature.

propositions.name: law_is_differential_equation
propositions.statement: A physical law is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow, expressible as a differential equation.
propositions.quote: For us a law is something quite different; it is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow; in a word, it is a differential equation.

propositions.name: today_and_tomorrow_shared
propositions.statement: The notions of to-day and to-morrow used to formulate physical law are shared across all observers who apply the law.
propositions.quote: For us a law is something quite different; it is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow; in a word, it is a differential equation.

propositions.name: conservation_of_energy
propositions.statement: The principle of the conservation of energy, or Mayer's principle, holds for the universe considered as a machine.
propositions.quote: the principle of the conservation of energy suffices to determine for us the most interesting point.

propositions.name: degradation_of_energy
propositions.statement: Carnot's principle, the degradation of energy, is a general principle governing physical phenomena.
propositions.quote: Carnot's principle, or the principle of the degradation of energy.

propositions.name: action_equals_reaction
propositions.statement: Newton's principle of the equality of action and reaction is a general principle of physics.
propositions.quote: Newton's principle, or the principle of the equality of action and reaction.

propositions.name: principle_of_relativity
propositions.statement: The laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation.
propositions.quote: The principle of relativity, according to which the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation

propositions.name: no_means_to_detect_translation
propositions.statement: There is no means of discerning whether or not one is carried along in a uniform motion of translation.
propositions.quote: so that we have not and can not have any means of discerning whether or not we are carried along in such a motion.

propositions.name: stationary_observer_meaningful
propositions.statement: The distinction between a stationary observer and one in uniform translation is a coherent one to state, even though no experiment can decide between them.
propositions.quote: the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation

propositions.name: uniform_translation_well_defined
propositions.statement: The notion of a uniform motion of translation is well-defined as a state applying to an observer.
propositions.quote: an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation; so that we have not and can not have any means of discerning whether or not we are carried along in such a motion.

propositions.name: conservation_of_mass
propositions.statement: The principle of the conservation of mass, or Lavoisier's principle, is a general principle of physics.
propositions.quote: The principle of the conservation of mass, or Lavoisier's principle.

propositions.name: principle_of_least_action
propositions.statement: The principle of least action is a general principle applicable across physical phenomena.
propositions.quote: I will add the principle of least action.

propositions.name: few_principles_suffice
propositions.statement: Application of five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena suffices to learn all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.
propositions.quote: The application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.

propositions.name: ether_transmits_both
propositions.statement: The ether transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations.
propositions.quote: we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations

propositions.name: ether_exists_as_medium
propositions.statement: There is a medium, the ether, in which optical and electrical perturbations propagate.
propositions.quote: We know nothing as to what the ether is, how its molecules are disposed, whether they attract or repel each other; but we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations

propositions.name: simultaneous_transmission_meaningful
propositions.statement: It is meaningful to say that the ether transmits optical and electrical perturbations at the same time.
propositions.quote: we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations

propositions.name: transmission_follows_mechanics
propositions.statement: The transmission of perturbations by the ether must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics.
propositions.quote: we know that this transmission must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics, and that suffices us for the establishment of the equations of the electromagnetic field.

propositions.name: principles_are_generalized_experiments
propositions.statement: The general principles of physics are results of experiments boldly generalized and derive their certainty from that generality.
propositions.quote: These principles are results of experiments boldly generalized; but they seem to derive from their very generality a high degree of certainty.

propositions.name: verification_multiplies_certainty
propositions.statement: The more general a principle, the more opportunities to check it, and multiplied verifications end by leaving no place for doubt.
propositions.quote: the more general they are, the more frequent are the opportunities to check them, and the verifications multiplying, taking the most varied, the most unexpected forms, end by no longer leaving place for doubt.

propositions.name: central_forces_imply_principles
propositions.statement: The hypothesis of central forces contained the conservation of energy, the conservation of masses, the equality of action and reaction, and the law of least action as necessary consequences.
propositions.quote: it involved both the conservation of energy and that of masses, and the equality of action and reaction, and the law of least action, which appeared, it is true, not as experimental truths, but as theorems

propositions.name: principles_now_experimental_truths
propositions.statement: The general principles are now regarded as experimental truths rather than as theorems following from the hypothesis of central forces.
propositions.quote: Thus they came to be regarded as experimental truths; the conception of central forces became then a useless, support, or rather an embarrassment, since it made the principles partake of its hypothetical character.

propositions.name: universe_as_machine
propositions.statement: The universe can be treated as a machine, most of whose parts are hidden, yet governed by principles that apply to the observable parts.
propositions.quote: The universe is also a machine, much more complicated than all those of industry, of which almost all the parts are profoundly hidden from us; but in observing the motion of those that we can see, we are able, by the aid of this principle, to draw conclusions which remain true whatever may be the details of the invisible mechanism which animates them.

propositions.name: hidden_mechanism_irrelevant
propositions.statement: Conclusions drawn from general principles about observable motion remain true whatever the details of the invisible mechanism.
propositions.quote: we are able, by the aid of this principle, to draw conclusions which remain true whatever may be the details of the invisible mechanism which animates them.

propositions.name: gear_ratio_from_visible_wheels
propositions.statement: By observing that the final wheel turns ten times less quickly than the initial wheel one can conclude that a couple applied to the one will be balanced by a couple ten times greater applied to the other.
propositions.quote: We easily ascertain that the final wheel turns ten times less quickly than the initial wheel, since these two wheels are visible; we are able thence to conclude that a couple applied to the one will be balanced by a couple ten times greater applied to the other.

propositions.name: rotational_speeds_comparable
propositions.statement: The rates at which the initial and final wheels turn are quantities that can be directly compared as a ratio.
propositions.quote: We easily ascertain that the final wheel turns ten times less quickly than the initial wheel, since these two wheels are visible

propositions.name: couples_compensate_in_interior
propositions.statement: Whatever the interior mechanism of a machine, the compensation of forces required by conservation of energy can not fail to occur.
propositions.quote: For that there is no need to penetrate the mechanism of this equilibrium and to know how the forces compensate each other in the interior of the machine; it suffices to be assured that this compensation can not fail to occur.

propositions.name: atoms_transmit_heat_without_moving
propositions.statement: In Fourier's theory atoms act at a distance to mutually transmit heat while they never budge.
propositions.quote: in it are indeed atoms acting at a distance one upon the other; they mutually transmit heat, but they do not attract, they never budge.

propositions.name: at_rest_is_definite
propositions.statement: It is meaningful to say of the atoms in Fourier's theory that they never budge, treating rest as a definite state.
propositions.quote: they mutually transmit heat, but they do not attract, they never budge.

propositions.name: orbits_regular_laws
propositions.statement: Material points describe orbits according to regular laws analogous to those of celestial mechanics.
propositions.quote: There also we should see material points, separated from one another by intervals, enormous in comparison with their dimensions, and describing orbits according to regular laws.

propositions.name: inverse_square_astronomical
propositions.statement: In the astronomic universe, masses attract each other inversely as the square of the distance, and this attraction is the sole force influencing their movements.
propositions.quote: These points attract each other inversely as the square of the distance, and this attraction is the sole force which influences their movements.

propositions.name: physics_born_of_celestial
propositions.statement: Mathematical physics was born of celestial mechanics at the end of the eighteenth century.
propositions.quote: Mathematical physics, as we know, was born of celestial mechanics, which gave birth to it at the end of the eighteenth century, at the moment when it itself attained its complete development.

propositions.name: principles_derived_from_data
propositions.statement: The enunciation of the principles has been modified by comparison with the data of experience, thereby extending and consolidating them.
propositions.quote: They have been compared with the data of experience, it has been seen how it was necessary to modify their enunciation to adapt them to these data; thereby they have been extended and consolidated.

propositions.name: capillarity_is_attraction_case
propositions.statement: Capillarity can be regarded as a particular case of universal gravitation, being constructed on the model of central forces between atoms.
propositions.quote: he regards it only as a particular case of attraction, or, as he says, of universal gravitation, and no one is astonished to find it in the middle of one of the five volumes of the 'Mécanique céleste.'

propositions.name: crisis_indicates_transformation
propositions.statement: There are indications of a serious crisis in mathematical physics, as if an approaching transformation of the science can be expected.
propositions.quote: there are indications of a serious crisis, as if we might expect an approaching transformation.

propositions.name: principles_hold_across_phenomena
propositions.statement: The same general principles apply uniformly across the different physical phenomena.
propositions.quote: The application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.
